meta.title: Lapar Smart: QR Menu Ordering System
meta.author: Abdul Rashid Alias (B24030058)

slides.title: Lapar Smart
slides.subtitle: QR Menu Ordering System for Lazaria Cafe, FAMA
meta: BIT4008 Undergraduate Project, Malaysia University of Science and Technology
slides.notes: Introduce the project: a QR-accessed mobile web application that replaces verbal ordering at the Lazaria Cafe counter.

slides.title: Ordering at the counter costs staff their break
slides.lead: Lazaria Cafe takes orders by voice at the counter. A questionnaire answered by 30 FAMA administrative assistants shows what that costs.

stats.label: waited 11 minutes or longer in the queue
received a wrong order at least once
want to pre-order catering for meetings

slides.note: Source: questionnaire, N = 30 (Table 3.1 of the report)
slides.notes: Long queues, misheard orders, no way to track an order, and meeting catering arranged by phone.

slides.title: One aim, four objectives
slides.lead: Design and develop a QR-accessed mobile web application for menu ordering at Lazaria Cafe, FAMA.

cards.head: QR ordering
cards.text: Staff scan a QR code, view the daily menu and place an order for collection.

cards.head: Admin module
cards.text: The cafe admin updates the daily menu and the status of every order.

cards.head: Order-ready alert
cards.text: An in-app alert on the status page and an email sent through Gmail.

cards.head: Meeting-room orders
cards.text: A Chief Clerk pre-orders a catering package and is emailed at every status.

slides.title: Commercial QR systems leave a gap
slides.note: Not stated: the vendor pages reviewed do not mention the feature. The three products are POS platforms built for restaurants, not for an in-house staff cafe.
slides.notes: Research gap: a lightweight system with a daily menu, meeting-room pre-orders and order tracking with an alert, without a POS subscription.

slides.title: Agile Scrum in six sprints over ten weeks
slides.note: One developer acting as product owner, Scrum Master and developer, with a self-review at the end of every sprint.
slides.notes: Scrum gave room for re-planning after each sprint review.

slides.title: Three kinds of user, fourteen use cases
slides.lead: 15 functional and 4 non-functional requirements, each traced to a use case and a pair of tests.

cards.head: FAMA Staff
cards.text: Scan the QR code, browse the menu, place a counter order and track it. No login.

cards.head: Chief Clerk (CC)
cards.text: Registers and logs in with a Staff ID to order meeting-room catering.

cards.head: Cafe Admin
cards.text: Manages the daily menu, orders, order status and Cafe Admin accounts.

slides.notes: The Chief Clerk is a specialisation of FAMA Staff in the use case diagram.

slides.title: A three-tier architecture on free cloud tiers

points.head: Email
points.text: Gmail SMTP for alerts and resets

slides.notes: Turso replaced a local SQLite file because the Vercel file system is not persistent.

slides.title: Staff order from their phone in three steps
bullets: Scan the QR code. The daily menu opens with no login.
Choose items and quantities from today's menu.
Review the order and enter Staff ID, name, department, phone and email.
The server re-reads every price, so the browser is never trusted.
slides.notes: Use cases Scan QR Code, View Daily Menu, Place Order and Review Order.

slides.title: The order is tracked until it is ready
bullets: Four statuses: Pending, Preparing, Ready and Completed.
The status page refreshes every 3 seconds and shows an alert at Ready.
An email is sent through Gmail, so the alert arrives even when the page is closed.
Payment is made at the counter on collection.

slides.title: Chief Clerks reserve catering for meeting rooms
bullets: The Meeting Order button leads to the Chief Clerk login.
Each package lists its food and its beverages by the jug.
The Chief Clerk chooses the room, the date and time, and the quantity.
An email follows at Pending, Preparing, Ready and Completed.
At Ready, cafe staff deliver the order to the meeting room.
slides.notes: Use case Reserve Meeting Room Order. Only an account with the CC role can see the packages.

slides.title: The cafe admin runs the day from one dashboard
bullets: View and filter counter and meeting-room orders.
Move an order to the next status with one click.
Add, hide or delete items on the daily menu.
Manage Cafe Admin accounts, with registration and password reset by email.
slides.notes: Use cases View Orders, Update Order Status, Mark Order Completed, Update Daily Menu and Manage Cafe Admins.

slides.title: Security is built into every request

cards.head: Passwords and sessions
cards.text: Salted password hashes and a signed session cookie for admins and Chief Clerks.

cards.head: Access by role
cards.text: Admin pages need an admin login. Meeting orders need a Chief Clerk login.

cards.head: Server-side validation
cards.text: Prices are re-read from the database and every staff detail is checked.

cards.head: Data integrity
cards.text: Parameterised SQL, foreign keys, HTTPS and secrets kept in environment variables.

slides.notes: Section 4.4 of the report. Known limitations are listed in Section 4.4.5.

slides.title: Every test case passed on the final build
slides.lead: Each of the fourteen use cases has one functional and one regression test, run through a real browser.

stats.label: manual test cases passed, 14 functional and 14 regression
command runs the whole suite, on every push

slides.note: Build 7cf361b, tested on 9 November 2026 (Chapter 5 and Appendix C)
slides.notes: Gmail is replaced by a stub in the automated tests. Delivery was shown separately on the production deployment.

slides.title: Fast enough for the lunch-hour queue
slides.lead: Measured on the production deployment after the function was moved next to the database.

stats.label: menu load, against a target of under 3 s
order submission, against a target of under 5 s
worst-case delay of the in-app alert
menu load before the fix, now about 0.2 s

slides.note: Means from warm instances on one network, 9 November 2026. Cold starts were not measured.
slides.notes: The delay came from the function running in Washington while the database is in Mumbai.

slides.title: Three of four quality requirements are verified
rows: User acceptance test, not carried out
Timed requests on the production deployment
85 simultaneous orders on a local database, none lost
slides.note: All fourteen use cases are marked Achieved in the traceability matrix (Table 5.5).
slides.notes: A UAT with 10 to 15 FAMA staff and the SUS questionnaire is recommended as future work.

slides.title: What works today, and what does not yet

left.head: Strengths
items: Orders are placed from a phone, not in a queue
Alerts in the app and by email
Daily menu and order status in one dashboard
Meeting-room catering with a Chief Clerk login

right.head: Limitations
items: Payment is still made at the counter
No user acceptance test has been run
The in-app alert needs the status page open
Load was tested on a local database only

slides.title: Next steps for a complete ordering service

cards.head: Online payment
cards.text: Add an e-wallet or payment gateway so staff can pay in the app.

cards.head: Verified identity
cards.text: Check staff identity and approve Chief Clerk registrations.

cards.head: Push alerts
cards.text: Deliver alerts with Web Push or as a Progressive Web App.

cards.head: User acceptance test
cards.text: Test with FAMA staff and run a production-scale load test.

slides.title: Scan, Order & Enjoy
slides.subtitle: Objectives 1, 2 and 4 are achieved. Objective 3 is achieved with an in-app alert and an email alert.
slides.notes: Open the production site for the live demonstration.
